title: Kiro unifies its IDE, terminal, web and mobile agents behind one harness
friendlyTitle: Kiro now uses the same AI agent across all its apps
summary: Kiro replaced separate TypeScript, Rust and Python agent implementations with one standalone harness shared across its IDE, CLI, web and iOS clients. The move standardizes sessions, permissions, tools and configuration so work can move between local and cloud environments more consistently.
friendlySummary: Kiro’s coding helper now shares one core system across the IDE, terminal, web and mobile app. Sessions and permissions can behave more consistently everywhere.
whyItMatters: A shared agent core reduces duplicated bugs and inconsistent safety rules across interfaces. Product teams building assistants for several surfaces can borrow the architecture: keep clients thin, centralize the agent contract and make sessions portable.
friendlyWhyItMatters: One shared agent is easier to improve and safer to manage than several different versions. It can also let users continue work on another device.
